prompt: A company has $1{,}500$ employees, $900$ of them full-time and $600$ part-time. HR takes a stratified sample of $60$ employees, with the strata represented in proportion to their sizes. How many full-time employees are in the sample?
hint: "In proportion to their sizes" means the sample has the same full-time fraction as the company.

hints.text: "In proportion to their sizes" means the sample has the same full-time fraction as the company.
Full-time fraction: $\frac{900}{1500} = 0.6$. Apply that to the sample of $60$.

explanation: Full-time employees make up $\frac{900}{1500} = 60$ percent of the company.
A proportional stratified sample keeps that share: $60$ percent of $60$ is $36$.
So $36$ full-time and $24$ part-time employees are sampled.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use a sampling rate
steps: The overall rate is $\frac{60}{1500} = \frac{1}{25}$: one employee in every 25.
Apply it to the full-time stratum: $\frac{900}{25} = 36$.
